bull_bear.body: Focus on organic capacity expansion and product development; no dividend, buyback, or M&A mentioned; technical fee payments to Meritor continue as revenue-linked arrangement.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Export market volatility; low-floor bus regulation uncertainty delaying product launch; dependency on Ashok Leyland (~60% revenue); non-MHCV segment underperformance; raw material cost sensitivity.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and proactive; management emphasizes operational agility, capacity readiness, and product pipeline; acknowledges export headwinds but attributes underperformance to mix, not share loss; tone is optimistic on FY27 upside if OEM demand materializes.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The INR11.9cr wage code charge is a one-time PBT impact, not recurring; MS185 traction is not new volume but replacement of older axles, with only 5-10% incremental share gain potential; export decline is industry-wide, not company-specific; bus axle delay is strategic, not technical.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- 43+ years of experience and market insight in Indian and Asian commercial-vehicle axle markets
- Technology partnership with Meritor Heavy Vehicle Systems LLC, USA, supporting product engineering, validation and testing
- MS185 flagship axle platform ramped up with additional customers during FY26, providing a competitive advantage
- Quality culture built on TPM, Built-in Quality, 5S and Six Sigma methodologies with a zero-defect focus
- Advanced manufacturing facilities - Face Hob gear-cutting machines, robotic welding, and a new Industry 4.0-enabled axle assembly line with digital interlocks and robotic painting
- Broad domestic client base with expanding global footprint; e-Axle technology capability supporting EV manufacturing
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Industry / cyclicality risk — Business is closely linked to the performance of the automotive sector; changes in customer demand, regulatory developments or shifts in consumer trends may impact demand pipelines and revenue visibility.
- Cost inflation / raw material risk — Raw material prices are subject to global supply chain dynamics and commodity fluctuations, which may result in inflationary pressures and impact margins.
- Technology risk — In a rapidly evolving automotive landscape, inability to adapt to changing technological requirements may impact product relevance and competitiveness.
- People / talent risk — Growth depends on the availability and retention of skilled talent; challenges in attracting, developing and retaining employees may impact productivity and organisational performance.
- Dependency on JV-partner affiliate for commercial and engineering services — Under an MoU and Services Agreement with Meritor HVS (India) Limited (effective April 1, 2025, extended via addendum to April 30, 2027), the Company sells directly to OEMs but obtains marketing, business development, product technology, engineering/product development, account management and programme-management services from Meritor HVS (India) Limited, creating reliance on a related party for key commercial and technical functions.

business.body: Automotive Axles Limited (AAL) is a joint venture between the Kalyani Group (India) and Cummins Inc. (USA), established in 1981, specialising in Rear Drive Axle Assemblies, S-Cam actuated quick-change air brakes and tag axles for vehicles in the 7 to 55 tonne gross vehicle weight range. Its product portfolio also covers front steer axles, defence axles, off-highway axles, non-drive axles, drum/disc brakes and crown wheel pinions. Customers span light, medium and heavy commercial vehicle OEMs, military/defence and off-highway vehicle makers, both in India and across export markets.

- **Non-Drive Axles:** Non-Drive Axles
- **Brakes:** S-Cam actuated quick-change air brakes, Drum Brakes, Disc Brakes
- **Other:** Defence Axles, Tag Axles, Crown Wheel Pinions

outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Most of order book converted in Q3; no backlog disclosed; capacity aligned with current demand.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: MS185 tandem axle gaining traction; new tipper axle in pilot production; global high-horsepower axle portfolio ready for localization post-2028; potential entry into low-floor bus axle market post-OCT26 regulation clarity.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Complete the ongoing capacity expansion programme while introducing advanced manufacturing technologies that further strengthen productivity, efficiency and quality performance
- Strengthen position in targeted growth segments and accelerate technology-led product development
- Strengthen global supply strategy, with exports expected to play an increasingly important role in the growth journey, supporting both domestic demand and emerging export opportunities
- Expand presence in defence, off-highway and advanced mobility applications, including e-axle and next-generation drivetrain technologies
- Continue manufacturing transformation through automation, digitalisation and advanced manufacturing technologies (robotic welding, advanced inspection systems, furnace modernisation, intelligent material handling, Industry 4.0-enabled processes)
- Maintain focus on operational excellence and profitability alongside growth initiatives
- Company follows a Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy (per SEBI LODR Regulation 43A) and has increased its per-share dividend payout year-on-year - Rs 32/share (320%) recommended for FY26 versus Rs 30.50/share (305%) paid for FY25 - subject to shareholder approval at the AGM. Management also highlights maintaining a strong balance sheet and healthy cash generation, which it says enables the Company to invest confidently in future growth opportunities (including the ongoing capacity expansion programme) alongside returning cash to shareholders.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The company is progressing the next phase of its capacity expansion programme, expected to be completed by the end of calendar year 2026, which will enhance capacity and introduce advanced manufacturing technologies to further strengthen productivity, efficiency and quality performance. Alongside this, the company accelerated its manufacturing transformation through investments in automation, digitalisation and advanced manufacturing technologies, including robotic welding, advanced inspection systems, furnace modernisation, intelligent material handling and Industry 4.0-enabled processes. As part of energy-conservation initiatives during FY26, the company converted its LPG-fired furnace to an electrical Holographic Continuous Carbonization Furnace (HCCF), supported by installation of a 2,000 KVA transformer, a 1,500 KVA diesel generator and associated HT/LT panels, alongside VFD installation, IE4 motor replacements and LED lighting upgrades across its plants; total capital investment on energy conservation equipment during FY26 was Rs 110.8 million. The company also continued focus on absorption of advanced gear-cutting technology to enhance product quality in gear and axle manufacturing.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Industry is witnessing a gradual shift towards higher-tonnage vehicles and tractor-trailer configurations, driven by evolving freight economics and productivity requirements; the company's built-up portfolio of heavy-duty axle solutions positions it favourably to participate in this transition
- India's growth fundamentals - infrastructure development, expanding industrial activity, rising freight movement and increasing manufacturing investments - provide a strong foundation for sustained growth in the commercial vehicle ecosystem
- Company remains well positioned to capitalise on emerging opportunities, supported by its strong presence in drive axle and braking solutions, deep engineering capabilities and long-standing OEM relationships, with continued focus on product reliability, cost competitiveness and operational excellence
- Policy initiatives such as PLI schemes, vehicle scrappage policy implementation and logistics efficiency improvements are expected to strengthen the long-term outlook for the automotive and auto component sectors
- MS185 advanced axle programme continued to gain traction across leading OEMs during the year, a key highlight of FY26 performance
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Automotive Axles Limited delivered strong Q3FY26 performance driven by volume conversion and margin expansion, despite export and non-MHCV headwinds; the company is strategically positioned to capture future growth through new products like MS185 and capacity expansion, with near-term upside tied to OEM inventory drawdown and bus axle regulatory clarity.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: A joint venture between Kalyani Group and Cummins Inc. (USA), Automotive Axles Limited is an Indian manufacturer of rear drive axles, air brakes and axle assemblies for commercial, off-highway and defence vehicles.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Automotive Axles Limited (AAL) is a joint venture between the Kalyani Group (India) and Cummins Inc. (USA), established in 1981, specialising in Rear Drive Axle Assemblies, S-Cam actuated quick-change air brakes and tag axles for vehicles in the 7 to 55 tonne gross vehicle weight range. Its product portfolio also covers front steer axles, defence axles, off-highway axles, non-drive axles, drum/disc brakes and crown wheel pinions. Customers span light, medium and heavy commercial vehicle OEMs, military/defence and off-highway vehicle makers, both in India and across export markets.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Meritor Heavy Vehicle System LLC — JV: Entity having joint control over the Company; AAL's technology partner (JV between Kalyani Group and Cummins/Meritor).
- Meritor Inc, Troy — related party: Holding company of Meritor Heavy Vehicle System LLC; entity having joint control over AAL.
- BF Investments Limited, Pune — related party: Entity having joint control over the Company (Kalyani Group investment entity).
- Meritor HVS (India) Limited — related party: Enterprise controlled/significantly influenced by the Joint Venturer (Meritor) with which AAL transacts; also an enterprise over which KMP have significant influence.
- Bharat Forge Limited — related party: Enterprise over which key management personnel (Dr. B N Kalyani, also Executive Director of Bharat Forge) have significant influence; part of the Kalyani Group.
- Parola Renewables Private Limited — associate: 26% shareholding held by AAL; does not participate in AAL's Business Responsibility initiatives per BRSR.
- Torrent Surya Urja 3 Private Limited — associate: 26% shareholding held by AAL; does not participate in AAL's Business Responsibility initiatives per BRSR.
- Axletech India Private Limited — related party: Enterprise controlled/jointly controlled/significantly influenced by the Joint Venturer (Meritor), with which AAL had transactions.
- Synise Technologies Limited — related party: Enterprise controlled/jointly controlled/significantly influenced by the Joint Venturer (Meritor), with which AAL had transactions.
- Valvoline Cummins Private Limited — related party: Enterprise controlled/jointly controlled/significantly influenced by the Joint Venturer (Cummins side of the JV), with which AAL had transactions.
- K Drive Mobility Solutions Private Limited — related party: Formerly known as AAM India Manufacturing Corp (renamed w.e.f. July 1, 2025); enterprise linked to the Joint Venturer group.
- Meritor group global affiliates (Meritor Heavy Vehicle Systems Cameri Spa; Xuzhou Meritor Axle Co. Ltd.; Meritor HVS LLC - Morristown, Florence, Troy; Meritor HVS Inc., Fletcher; Meritor HVS AB, Sweden; Meritor HVS Australia; Sistemas Automotrices de Mexico; Meritor Laurinberg Speciality; Meritor Aftermarket Switzerland AG; Meritor do Brasil Sistemas Automotivos Ltda.) — related party: Enterprises controlled/jointly controlled/significantly influenced by the Joint Venturer (Meritor), with which AAL had transactions.

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Most of order book converted in Q3; no backlog disclosed; capacity aligned with current demand.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Q4FY26 revenue expected to be 5-10% higher than prior quarter; FY27 outlook remains cautious pending OEM inventory clarity at end-March; no formal revenue growth target provided.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: MS185 tandem axle gaining traction; new tipper axle in pilot production; global high-horsepower axle portfolio ready for localization post-2028; potential entry into low-floor bus axle market post-OCT26 regulation clarity.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Industry is witnessing a gradual shift towards higher-tonnage vehicles and tractor-trailer configurations, driven by evolving freight economics and productivity requirements; the company's built-up portfolio of heavy-duty axle solutions positions it favourably to participate in this transition
- India's growth fundamentals - infrastructure development, expanding industrial activity, rising freight movement and increasing manufacturing investments - provide a strong foundation for sustained growth in the commercial vehicle ecosystem
- Company remains well positioned to capitalise on emerging opportunities, supported by its strong presence in drive axle and braking solutions, deep engineering capabilities and long-standing OEM relationships, with continued focus on product reliability, cost competitiveness and operational excellence
- Policy initiatives such as PLI schemes, vehicle scrappage policy implementation and logistics efficiency improvements are expected to strengthen the long-term outlook for the automotive and auto component sectors
- MS185 advanced axle programme continued to gain traction across leading OEMs during the year, a key highlight of FY26 performance

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margin 12.9% (+52 bps QoQ, +93 bps YoY); PAT margin 7% (impacted by INR11.9cr wage code exceptional item); COGS trend improving due to lighter designs and supply chain optimization; technical fees with Meritor rose with revenue growth.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Focus on organic capacity expansion and product development; no dividend, buyback, or M&A mentioned; technical fee payments to Meritor continue as revenue-linked arrangement.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The company is progressing the next phase of its capacity expansion programme, expected to be completed by the end of calendar year 2026, which will enhance capacity and introduce advanced manufacturing technologies to further strengthen productivity, efficiency and quality performance. Alongside this, the company accelerated its manufacturing transformation through investments in automation, digitalisation and advanced manufacturing technologies, including robotic welding, advanced inspection systems, furnace modernisation, intelligent material handling and Industry 4.0-enabled processes. As part of energy-conservation initiatives during FY26, the company converted its LPG-fired furnace to an electrical Holographic Continuous Carbonization Furnace (HCCF), supported by installation of a 2,000 KVA transformer, a 1,500 KVA diesel generator and associated HT/LT panels, alongside VFD installation, IE4 motor replacements and LED lighting upgrades across its plants; total capital investment on energy conservation equipment during FY26 was Rs 110.8 million. The company also continued focus on absorption of advanced gear-cutting technology to enhance product quality in gear and axle manufacturing.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and proactive; management emphasizes operational agility, capacity readiness, and product pipeline; acknowledges export headwinds but attributes underperformance to mix, not share loss; tone is optimistic on FY27 upside if OEM demand materializes.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- 43+ years of experience and market insight in Indian and Asian commercial-vehicle axle markets
- Technology partnership with Meritor Heavy Vehicle Systems LLC, USA, supporting product engineering, validation and testing
- MS185 flagship axle platform ramped up with additional customers during FY26, providing a competitive advantage
- Quality culture built on TPM, Built-in Quality, 5S and Six Sigma methodologies with a zero-defect focus
- Advanced manufacturing facilities - Face Hob gear-cutting machines, robotic welding, and a new Industry 4.0-enabled axle assembly line with digital interlocks and robotic painting
- Broad domestic client base with expanding global footprint; e-Axle technology capability supporting EV manufacturing

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Export market volatility; low-floor bus regulation uncertainty delaying product launch; dependency on Ashok Leyland (~60% revenue); non-MHCV segment underperformance; raw material cost sensitivity.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: The INR11.9cr wage code charge is a one-time PBT impact, not recurring; MS185 traction is not new volume but replacement of older axles, with only 5-10% incremental share gain potential; export decline is industry-wide, not company-specific; bus axle delay is strategic, not technical.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Complete the ongoing capacity expansion programme while introducing advanced manufacturing technologies that further strengthen productivity, efficiency and quality performance
- Strengthen position in targeted growth segments and accelerate technology-led product development
- Strengthen global supply strategy, with exports expected to play an increasingly important role in the growth journey, supporting both domestic demand and emerging export opportunities
- Expand presence in defence, off-highway and advanced mobility applications, including e-axle and next-generation drivetrain …

themes.title: Railway rolling-stock & component capex
themes.need: A ~INR2.65 lakh cr Railways capital outlay and a pending ~1-lakh-wagon tender ('anytime this year' per JWL) drive rolling-stock, wheelsets, springs, castings, bogie components and interiors - with deep import-substitution (Neetu Yoshi 544434 castings; Airfloa 544516 interiors; Concord 543619 electronics). TITAGARH/TEXRAIL/JWL lead wagons; RVNL/IRCON/GPTINFRA on rail EPC.
themes.driver: Indian Railways large wagon tender award (next 1-2 quarters); wheelset plant ramp; Vande Bharat / Kavach orders.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.
